subject: kernel 0096: CPU-access tracking removes per-job cache maintenance; bridge flags requested
body: Measured c6k: ~2 ms/job is cache maintenance (clean+invalidate of ~16.5 MiB/job: the 16 MiB matrix heap + surfaces), GPU run ~0.1 ms. 0096 (host-only, gpu/build/kernel-p1-20261026/0096-*.patch): (1) ALLOC flags bit1 = GPU-ONLY: kernel refuses any CPU mapping of that buffer; it is cleaned once (zero fill) and then NEVER maintained. Please allocate heap, TLS/WLS, private-storage textures/buffers, MRT/resolve targets with flags|2 and never map them. Diagnostics that map the heap (tiler matrix, geometry trace) must allocate it WITHOUT bit1 (then it is maintained like today). Without the flag nothing breaks: a buffer that is never mapped is detected automatically (level 1). (2) Level 2 (boot-arg n2trk=2): IOSurface-imported buffers are no longer cleaned/invalidated per job. CPU access MUST be bracketed by IOSurfaceLock/IOSurfaceUnlock (kernel trapLock = acquire: invalidates only if the GPU wrote since; trapUnlock without ReadOnly = clean before next GPU read; FB present() acquires). So any frontend/bridge CPU write into an IOSurface-backed texture needs Lock(0)/Unlock(0) and any CPU readback after a command completes needs Lock(ReadOnly) after the wait. Shared-storage MTLBuffers/textures that are CPU-mapped keep today's per-job maintenance (listed buffers only). Please confirm no unbracketed CPU access to imported surfaces exists in render_encoder/tegu paths.
